dedupe_keys.name: astrolibrary spacemap conjunction assessment and collision avoidance library

description: AstroLibrary implements the SpaceMap method for real-time conjunction assessment and near-real-time collision avoidance among very large populations of space objects. Researchers at Hanyang University's Voronoi Diagram Research Center and the Korea Aerospace Research Institute developed it because catalogues of about ten thousand objects are already hard to screen and will grow by orders of magnitude with new constellations and debris. The method represents the spatiotemporal proximity of satellites in a Voronoi diagram, which the authors describe as a basis for space-time AI, and claims scalability to a million or more objects. Coverage is any Earth-orbit catalogue. Format and access: algorithms in C++ with RESTful APIs and Python packages, published on GitHub according to the open-access paper in the Journal of Space Safety Engineering (July 2024). Licence: the paper is CC BY-NC-ND; the software licence was not stated in the text read; free. Caveats: performance figures are the developers' own, and the repository address and its maintenance could not be checked from here. It supports optimisation of collision avoidance and hazard exposure studies of debris for satellite infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the ESA collision avoidance challenge dataset and the TraCSS conjunction assessment verification dataset, which can serve as test inputs.
